setup.name: daf-setup
setup.description: Project setup after `daf global-setup`: greenfield copies ~/.config/agent/scaffold into .agent/ (optional /grill-me later); brownfield runs inventory + interview then merge scaffold and populate PRD/glossary/architecture; verify-state.json; optional Cursor overlay. Use when the user says /setup or needs .agent/ in the project.

grill-me.name: daf-grill-me
grill-me.description: Phase-aware: in planning, skeptical PRD interview (one question at a time, assumption audit, stack recommendation). In developing or maintaining, realignment — resync intent with PRD/ARCHITECTURE/code/backlog without net-new scope unless asked. Use when the user says /grill-me or grill-me.

start.name: daf-start
start.description: Validates planning exit, sets phase to developing when ready, and kicks off the first developing session (read backlog, one goal question). Use when the user says /start or wants to begin building after planning.

how-it-works.name: daf-how-it-works
how-it-works.description: Technical implementation-precise explanation of a requested topic in this repo (flow, files, state) without code changes unless asked. Use when the user says /how-it-works or wants to understand how something works in the codebase.

ltm-checkup.name: daf-ltm-checkup
ltm-checkup.description: Reconciles .agent/ canon and code with external long-term memory (e.g. Notion via MCP): drift inventory, one question at a time, confirmed doc updates only. Use when the user says /ltm-checkup or wants LTM vs repo alignment.

new-feature.name: daf-new-feature
new-feature.description: Implements net-new product capability in **developing** phase (new commands, skills, flows) with acceptance checks; verification per phases/developing.md (taskCheck, verify-state, periodic codebase-check). Not for polish on existing behavior — use /improvement. In **maintaining**, use only when the user explicitly opts in. Use when the user says /new-feature or asks for scoped new capability while phase is developing.

issue.name: daf-issue
issue.description: Triages and fixes a reported issue in **developing** or **maintaining**: reproduce, root-cause fix (no band-aids), regression tests; verification per the current phase file. Use when the user says /issue or reports a bug to fix.

improvement.name: daf-improvement
improvement.description: Improves existing code, docs, or workflow at the root (refactor, clarity, patterns) — no copy-paste workarounds; not bugs (/issue) or net-new capability (/new-feature). Verification per the current phase file. Use when the user says /improvement or asks to make something existing better.

pivot.name: daf-pivot
pivot.description: Guides restructuring or redesign of an existing feature, concept, or architecture: from→to, blast radius, update GLOSSARY/ARCHITECTURE/PRD, migration plan, then implement per the current phase file in developing or maintaining. Not incremental polish (/improvement), net-new capability (/new-feature), brownfield DAF adoption (/setup), or open exploration (/discuss). Use when the user says /pivot or decides to redesign something that already exists.

discuss.name: daf-discuss
discuss.description: Explores a topic, idea, or direction through dialogue — brainstorm and tradeoffs without implementing. Not bugs (/issue), ranked build plans (/improvement), PRD interviews (/grill-me), or net-new builds (/new-feature). Use when the user says /discuss or wants to think through something before committing.

backlog-add.name: daf-backlog-add
backlog-add.description: Appends a follow-up to repo-root BACKLOG.md under ## Open without implementing. Any phase. Use when the user says /backlog-add or wants to park work for later.

backlog-work.name: daf-backlog-work
backlog-work.description: In developing or maintaining: pick an open BACKLOG.md item, classify and implement (new-feature/improvement/issue/pivot bar), then on user acceptance remove from backlog and append a fading artifact to LOGBACK.md. Use when the user says /backlog-work or wants to build the next backlog item.

remember.name: daf-remember
remember.description: Saves a user-stated standing instruction to .agent/memory/remember.md for this project. Not retro takeaways (/retro) or discovered gotchas. Use when the user says /remember or asks the agent to always follow a project rule.

retro.name: daf-retro
retro.description: Captures short retro notes for memory/learnings or gotchas after non-trivial work. Use when the user says /retro or asks for a brief retrospective.

phase-transition.name: daf-phase-transition
phase-transition.description: Validates planning exit checklist before editing config.phase to developing or maintaining (same rules as validatePlanningExit in the DAF repo). Use when the user says /phase-transition or asks to leave planning.

remove.name: daf-remove
remove.description: Removes DAF from the current repo: .agent/, DAF bootstrap AGENTS.md, and .cursor/rules/daf.mdc after explicit confirmation. Not machine-wide — use /remove-global. Use when the user says /remove or wants to strip project agent structure.

remove-global.name: daf-remove-global
remove-global.description: Uninstalls machine-wide DAF: deletes ~/.config/agent (or DAFE_GLOBAL_ROOT) and ~/.cursor/skills/daf-* folders from skill-manifest after explicit confirmation. Per-repo .agent/ remains until /remove. Use when the user says /remove-global or wants to uninstall global-setup output.
